I will plant my cowpea using seed I saved from last season because the improved varieties at the agro-dealer shop are too expensive for me this year. Since beans are a legume that can fix nitrogen, I will not buy chemical fertilizer, but I will spread goat manure from our animals to strengthen the soil. I must buy pesticide because the pod borers and aphids here always attack cowpea, and without spraying I will lose much of the crop. We depend on the rains completely, so I will not irrigate; my family will work about 40 days on this plot, and I will hire about 5 extra labor days at harvest when the work is heaviest.
